Journalism and AI:
Addressing Fears, Anxieties, and Concerns
Wednesday, October 28, 2026
10:00 AM PT / 1:00 PM ET
Free to attend
In this webinar panel, three seasoned journalists —
Taylor Lorenz
,
Alexandra Marvar
, and
Brian Merchant
— will share how media workers can navigate AI tools and the various ways in which this technology has transformed the industry.
This panel will touch upon how legacy media outlets are coming up with AI rules, and what writers can do to protect their work. In addition, the panelists will discuss larger questions about how AI has changed the industry: Is it possible to integrate these tools in a workflow without plagiarizing other writers' work? Is there a double standard of media outlets banning freelancers from using these tools, while editors use in-house AI tools? What does it mean to have original prose in a time when LLMs can mimic style?
Register
here
.
ICYMI:
Bridget Read on writing a zeitgeisty feature.
Astead Herndon on stepping out of the political media bubble.
Katie Notopoulos on tech reporting.
OTHER RESOURCES
▶ Add to the Rate-Sharing Database
The
Freelance Solidarity Project
maintains an ongoing
Rate Sharing Database
to build a clearer picture of freelance pay—and, ultimately, change how we are paid. Add your rates, and help build a more equitable future for freelancers in the industry.
The Institute for Independent Journalists have opened registration for the
Fall 2026 Business of Freelancing course
, offered from Oct. 1 through Nov. 19.
This eight-week, live online course provides a comprehensive foundation in the business of freelance journalism and has sold out every time they’ve presented it. Each session combines real-world strategy with personalized guidance, covering topics such as rate setting, time and income management, client relationships, and long-term planning.
Registration is $249 before Sept 24, and $299 after.
They’ve also announced
their lineup of webinars
for freelancers, featuring assigning editors, fellowship directors, and independent creators. Each webinar runs from 12-1:15 pm EST and costs $30.
